title: RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has become a main technique for alleviating hallucinations in large language models (LLMs). Despite the integration of RAG, LLMs may still present unsupported or contradictory claims to the retrieved contents. In order to develop effective hallucination prevention strategies under RAG, it is important to create benchmark datasets that can measure the extent of hallucination. This paper presents RAGTruth, a corpus tailored for analyzing word-level hallucinations in various domains and tasks within the standard RAG frameworks for LLM applications. RAGTruth comprises nearly 18,000 naturally generated responses from diverse LLMs using RAG. These responses have undergone meticulous manual annotations at both the individual cases and word levels, incorporating evaluations of hallucination intensity. We not only benchmark hallucination frequencies across different LLMs, but also critically assess the effectiveness of several existing hallucination detection methodologies. Furthermore, we show that using a high-quality dataset such as RAGTruth, it is possible to finetune a relatively small LLM and achieve a competitive level of performance in hallucination detection when compared to the existing prompt-based approaches using state-of-the-art large language models such as GPT-4.

claims.text: RAGTruth comprises 17,790 naturally generated responses from six diverse LLMs across question answering, data-to-text writing, and news summarization tasks.
Fine-tuning a Llama-2-13B model on RAGTruth training data achieves a response-level hallucination detection F1 score of 78.7%.
Prompt-based GPT-4-turbo achieves a response-level hallucination detection F1 score of 63.4%.
Fine-tuning Llama-2-13B on RAGTruth achieves a character-level span detection F1 score of 52.7%, outperforming GPT-4-turbo's F1 score of 28.3%.

Selecting candidate LLM responses with zero detected hallucination spans using the finetuned Llama-2-13B detector reduces response hallucination rates by 63.2% for Llama-2-7B/Mistral-7B and by 51.0% for GPT-3.5/GPT-4.
Baseless information generation is significantly more prevalent in RAG responses than direct factual contradiction with context.

limitations.text: Existing datasets for LLM hallucination detection are predominantly synthetic or small-scale and lack focus on RAG scenarios.
Current detection methods, including the finetuned Llama-2-13B model, fall short of perfect span-level hallucination identification (achieving an overall span-level F1 of 52.7%).
The benchmark does not address all practical application scenarios and emerging sources of hallucination in RAG environments.

future_work.text: Development of improved fine-grained span-level hallucination detection and mitigation methodologies for RAG LLMs.

methodologies.name: RAGTruth Corpus Construction and Manual Annotation Pipeline
methodologies.description: Generated responses from 6 LLMs using natural prompts across 3 tasks, followed by manual word-level and span-level annotation using a 4-category hallucination taxonomy.

methodologies.name: Llama-2-13B Finetuning for Hallucination Detection
methodologies.description: Full parameter finetuning of Llama-2-13B on context-response pairs from RAGTruth to directly output hallucinated spans.
